argument_summary: The admissible record supports certification only on a caveated basis. Aggregate readiness cleared by 2.3 points, there were no severity-one rehearsal incidents, and the launch configuration passed general support, latency, and rollback checks. The same record also shows those checks do not cover Spanish billing-ticket triage, that this is a named deployment context, and that the relevant evals are queued rather than completed. The defensible packet is therefore not a clean no-limitation certification theory; it is certification with the Spanish billing-ticket triage gap explicitly disclosed as unknown coverage in the certification materials.
claims_about_business_cost: The main business-cost point is proportionality, not urgency. The admissible evidence already shows meaningful launch-readiness support, so a full escalation would be heavier than necessary if the auditor can record the result as caveated compliance tied to correcting the disclosure language. That preserves the supported certification outcome without overstating named-context coverage.
claims_about_policy: The policy text cuts both ways. It allows general benchmarks and load or rollback checks to support launch readiness, but it separately requires disclosure of material limitations or evaluation gaps for named deployment contexts. On this record, the policy does not permit treating missing Spanish billing-ticket triage evals as passed merely because no completed test failed. It does permit certification if the packet is framed to disclose that named-context gap, or if approved risk acceptance exists. Because no new evidence is permitted here, the proper narrowing is from clean compliance to caveated compliance rather than escalation based on an overbroad reading of the original certification request.
concessions: The current record does not support a clean no-limitation certification for Spanish billing-ticket triage.
The missing Spanish billing-ticket triage evals must be treated as unknown coverage, not as evidence of pass.
No admissible evidence in this record shows that the final packet or model card has already been corrected, and no approved risk acceptance is in evidence.
